claims.text: Proves the full Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer leading-term formula for every elliptic curve over ℚ whose full q-power Selmer group has corank zero or one for some prime q, including finiteness of the Tate–Shafarevich group.

claims.text: With result 006, this gives full BSD for a density-one set of quadratic twists of every elliptic curve over ℚ.

claims.text: Proves that every Dirichlet L-function, including $`\zeta(s)`$, is zero-free in $`\Re s\gt 7/8`$, resolving the quasi-Riemann hypothesis.
claims.rationale: Zeta and every Dirichlet L-function nonzero for Re s>7/8, all moduli and characters; pole exclusion is standard.

claims.text: The same half-plane is zero-free for every finite-order Hecke L-function over $`\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})`$.
claims.rationale: Hecke target covers finite-order characters over Q(sqrt-3) (unit-trivial residue characters; class number one) for Re s>7/8, pole excluded.

claims.text: A companion gives a different proof of the zero-free half-plane $`\Re s\gt 11/12`$.
claims.rationale: The 11/12 half-plane is implied by the stronger 7/8 targets; the alternative proof itself is not a statement and cannot be checked.

claims.text: Proves that no algorithm decides whether an integer-coefficient polynomial in an arbitrary number of variables has a rational zero, resolving Hilbert's tenth problem over ℚ negatively.
claims.rationale: CONTENTS.md links no Lean scope note for this family, so it has no formal side.

claims.text: Proves that Catalan's constant $`G=\sum_{j\ge0}(-1)^j/(2j+1)^2`$ is irrational.
claims.rationale: Target states irrationality of exactly the series defining G.

claims.text: Proves Goldfeld's conjecture for quadratic twists of every elliptic curve over ℚ: analytic ranks zero and one each have density 1/2, and the mean analytic rank tends to 1/2.
claims.rationale: CONTENTS.md links no Lean scope note for this family, so it has no formal side.

claims.text: Both statements order signed squarefree twist parameters by absolute value.
claims.rationale: CONTENTS.md links no Lean scope note for this family, so it has no formal side.

claims.text: Proves the ordinary two-point Chowla conjecture, with a bound $`O(X/(\log X)^c)`$ for Liouville correlation sums along fixed nonproportional affine forms, where c > 0 is absolute.
claims.rationale: Absolute c, form-dependent C, Liouville affine sums with nonproportional forms bounded by X/(log X)^c.

claims.text: More generally, proves the binary corrected Elliott conjecture for complex multiplicative functions bounded by one when one factor is uniformly nonpretentious against each fixed Dirichlet character times $`n^{it}`$ for $`|t|\le X`$.
claims.rationale: One-bounded multiplicative f1,f2, one uniformly nonpretentious against chi n^{it}, |t|<=N; ordinary correlation averages tend to zero.

claims.text: Proves that the rational Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra, with the Ihara bracket, is freely generated by one element in each odd weight 3, 5, 7, …, resolving the Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture.
claims.rationale: Graded Lie isomorphism from free Lie algebra on odd generators to rational solution space (antisymmetry, 3-term, pentagon) with Ihara bracket.

claims.text: Reconstructs function fields of transcendence degree at least two over algebraically closed constants from $`K^{\mathrm M}_1/\ell`$, $`K^{\mathrm M}_2/\ell`$, and their product.

claims.text: These data recover the perfect closure and constants when ℓ differs from the characteristic, and the original field and its named base in equal characteristic.

claims.text: Also proves Bogomolov–Pop reconstruction from abelian-by-central pro-ℓ Galois data away from the characteristic.

claims.rationale: Absolute C, any K>0, truncations 0<eps<=R<=1/(10^6 K), uniform L2 bound on Schwartz functions.

claims.rationale: Geometric-progression case only for the dyadic ratio, not every ratio.

claims.text: Resolves the planar centered-disk case of the Hajłasz–Onninen maximal-function regularity problem.
claims.rationale: Endpoint W^{1,1} gradient bound for the planar centered disk maximal function is stated.

claims.text: It belongs locally to $`W^{1,1}`$ and has a globally integrable weak gradient.
claims.rationale: Target includes W^{1,1}_loc membership and globally integrable weak gradient.

claims.rationale: Symmetric bound with Hanner equality and general bound with simplex equality, every n>=1.

claims.text: The corresponding sharp functional Mahler inequalities also hold.
claims.rationale: Scope note says functional Mahler inequalities are not included.

claims.text: For n ≥ 2, every symmetric polar product $`K\times K^\circ`$ in dimension $`2n`$ has Gromov width 4.
claims.rationale: n>=2, symmetric convex body: Gromov width of K x K polar equals 4.

claims.text: Proves Petty's projection-volume conjecture in the remaining dimensions n ≥ 4: ellipsoids uniquely minimize projection-body volume at fixed body volume.
claims.rationale: n>=4, all convex bodies, Petty bound with equality iff ellipsoid.

claims.text: Also establishes the full Lutwak–Petty projection inequalities.
claims.rationale: Scope note says other projection-body inequalities are not included.

claims.text: In contrast, products of simplices exceed Brannen's proposed simplex maximum for normalized projection-body volume by an exponential factor in every sufficiently large dimension.
claims.rationale: Only dimension 20 counterexample; exponential factor in all large dimensions is excluded per scope note.

claims.text: Resolves the planar and bounded-treewidth cases of the Gupta–Newman–Rabinovich–Sinclair conjecture.
claims.rationale: Universal planar L1 distortion and treewidth-dependent bound are both targets.

claims.text: Shortest-path metrics of finite connected graphs with arbitrary positive edge lengths embed into real L1 with universal distortion for planar graphs, and distortion depending only on treewidth for bounded-treewidth graphs.
claims.rationale: Finite connected graphs, positive edge lengths, L1 embeddings with constant C or C(k).

claims.text: The corresponding multicommodity flow–cut gaps are uniformly bounded.
claims.rationale: Multicommodity flow-cut gaps are not stated in any target or the scope note.

claims.text: Proves that the triangular lattice minimizes the lower limit of energy per particle for every nonnegative completely monotone potential of squared distance among locally finite planar configurations of centered-disk density one.
claims.rationale: Nonnegative completely monotone g, locally finite density-one configurations; liminf disk energy at least lattice energy.

claims.text: It also minimizes unit-background renormalized Riesz energies for $`0\lt s\lt 2`$ and Coulomb energy, resolving Sandier–Serfaty and the two-dimensional Brauchart–Hardin–Saff conjecture on the linear term of optimal spherical logarithmic energy.
claims.rationale: Riesz, Coulomb and spherical logarithmic energy results are not in targets or scope note.

claims.text: For Lebesgue volume it also proves the additive Lp Brunn–Minkowski inequality for full-dimensional origin-symmetric convex bodies throughout $`0\lt p\lt 1`$.
claims.rationale: L_p Brunn-Minkowski for 0<p<1 is not in the target or scope note.

claims.text: Determines the optimal worst-case covering density as $`\Theta(n\log n)`$, for both lattice and unrestricted translative coverings.
claims.rationale: Translative and lattice suprema both Theta(n log n) for large n.

claims.text: Every convex body in ℝn, n ≥ 2, admits a lattice covering of density at most $`Cn\log n`$; centrally symmetric examples in every sufficiently large dimension require at least $`cn\log n`$ even without the lattice restriction, for absolute $`c,C\gt 0`$.

claims.text: Proves a dimension-free logarithmic Sobolev inequality for centered log-concave densities with uniformly subgaussian linear marginals, with constant bounded by a universal multiple of the squared linear subgaussian parameter.

claims.text: In contrast, exact embeddings require worst-case dimension $`\Theta(n^2)`$ when p ≠ 2.
claims.rationale: Distortion 1: floor((n-1)/4)^2 <= dim <= C(n,2) for n>=9.

claims.text: Disproves the Projected Lax conjecture: some hyperbolicity cones are not spectrahedral shadows.
claims.rationale: Target only shows the cone is not a spectrahedron; failure to be a spectrahedral shadow (projected lift) is not stated.

claims.text: The examples admit no exact finite affine semidefinite lift, regardless of the number of auxiliary variables or the real coefficients used.
claims.rationale: No lifts with auxiliary variables are excluded in the target; only direct linear pencils.

claims.text: This also disproves the generalized Lax conjecture that every hyperbolicity cone is spectrahedral.
claims.rationale: Hyperbolic degree-20 polynomial whose cone is no PSD region of any linear pencil of any size.

claims.text: Proves that the sum of squared Gaussian first moments of any finite measurable partition is at most $`9/(8\pi)`$.
claims.rationale: Every finite measurable partition, any dimension, value <= 9/(8 pi).

claims.text: In dimension at least two, three planar sectors of angle $`2\pi/3`$, extended orthogonally, attain the bound.
claims.rationale: d>=2, propeller partition attains 9/(8 pi).

claims.text: Combined with the separate Unique Games theorem, this proves NP-hardness of improving the loss factor $`(8\pi/9)(1-1/k)`$ for identity-target kernel clustering with fixed k ≥ 3 on rational centered positive semidefinite inputs.
claims.rationale: Scope note says kernel-clustering consequences are not included.

claims.text: Proves that any finite sequence in the Euclidean unit ball of ℝd admits signs keeping every partial sum within $`C\sqrt d`$, independently of length.
claims.rationale: Signs with all prefix norms <= C sqrt d, absolute C, any length.

claims.text: Consequently every zero-sum family can be reordered with the same bound on unsigned partial sums.
claims.rationale: Zero-sum family has permutation with unsigned prefixes <= C sqrt d.

claims.text: A matching lower bound gives the optimal order $`S_2(d)=\Theta(\sqrt d)`$.
claims.rationale: Upper bound O(sqrt d) is stated; the matching lower bound is not in any target.

claims.text: The doubling constant is universal.
claims.rationale: Lambda is chosen before the Banach space, so universal.

claims.text: This answers the Lang–Plaut problem negatively, even for compact subsets of Hilbert space.
claims.rationale: Applying CompactBanach to Hilbert space gives compact counterexamples there.

claims.rationale: Least l1 distortion between exp(c sqrt(log d loglog d)) and exp(C ...) for large d.

claims.text: Insertions, deletions and substitutions have unit cost.
claims.rationale: Unit-cost edit distance is the definition used in E Alpha d.

claims.text: The constants are uniform over all finite alphabets with at least two symbols, even when the alphabet grows with d; binary words already force the lower bound.
claims.rationale: Constants uniform over all finite alphabets of size >=2; binary witness of common length gives lower bound.

claims.text: Covers the entire closed regular tetrahedron by finitely many cylinders with compact triangular perpendicular bases whose total area is less than half its smallest orthogonal projection area.
claims.rationale: MainAsymptotic gives a finite cover of the regular tetrahedron by compact triangular-base cylinders with totalArea < A_min/2.

claims.text: This disproves Bang's half-area cylinder-covering bound and the stronger directionwise normalized conjecture in dimension three.
claims.rationale: Strict cover below half minimum shadow refutes the half-area bound; NormalizedCounterexample and regular counterexample statements give relativeCost < 1/2.

claims.text: Proves that simplices uniquely maximize the isotropic constant among convex bodies in every dimension, resolving the strong isotropic constant conjecture.

claims.text: Proves Khot's Unique Games Conjecture.
claims.rationale: Polynomial reduction from 3SAT to unique games with completeness 1-eps and soundness delta for all small eps, delta; the delta<1/2 restriction is harmless.

claims.text: Independent direct reductions also establish NP-hardness, on unweighted graphs, of approximation beyond the Goemans–Williamson ratio for Max-Cut, below factor two for Vertex Cover, and within any fixed constant factor for Min-UnCut and directed feedback vertex set.
claims.rationale: Targets give unweighted gap reductions for Max-Cut beyond alphaGW, Vertex Cover below 2, Min-UnCut and DFVS for every fixed factor.

claims.rationale: Claim concerns proof method (use of PCP/Label Cover results); no formal statement encodes that dependence.

claims.text: Proves $`\mathsf L=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}`$, resolving derandomization for bounded-error logarithmic-space computation.
claims.rationale: Target states L = RL and RL = BPL in the explicit logspace machine model.

claims.text: An effective compiler converts each randomized polynomial-time logarithmic-space machine deciding a language with one-sided or two-sided error into a deterministic logarithmic-space decider with explicit polynomial running-time bounds.
claims.rationale: Class equality gives only existence of a deterministic decider; effective compiler and explicit running-time bounds are not stated, per scope note.

claims.text: Gives deterministic algorithms using $`2^{O((\log(L+2))^2)}`$ bit operations, for complete binary input length L, for ordinary mean-payoff games and two separate extensions.
claims.rationale: Target is a randomized (prob 7/8) quasipolynomial algorithm for ordinary mean-payoff winning sets only; deterministic algorithms and both extensions absent.

claims.text: They compute exact values and optimal positional strategies in ordinary games, the nonnegative expectation-of-liminf value set in turn-based stochastic games, and the winning set for nonnegative liminf mean payoff conjoined with parity.
claims.rationale: Only the zero-threshold winning set of ordinary games; exact values, positional strategies, stochastic and parity extensions are not stated.

claims.text: Signed rewards, rational chance probabilities, and parity priorities are unrestricted and binary-encoded.
claims.rationale: Signed binary-encoded weights covered; chance probabilities and parity priorities appear in no target.

claims.text: Proves Khot's 2-to-1 Games Conjecture with perfect completeness: for every fixed rational $`\delta\in(0,1)`$, it is NP-hard to distinguish satisfiable games from games whose optimum is at most δ, on explicit unweighted instances.
claims.rationale: For every rational delta in (0,1), polynomial reduction from 3SAT to unweighted 2-to-1 games with value 1 versus at most delta.

claims.text: The alphabet depends only on δ, and every right-hand label has exactly two preimages under each constraint map.
claims.rationale: Per scope note the reduction contract fixes an alphabet depending only on delta and exactly two preimages per label.

claims.text: It is NP-hard to color a three-colorable graph using any fixed number c ≥ 3 of colors.
claims.rationale: Taking delta < 1/c, independence number below delta n forces chromatic number above c; immediate corollary of the stated reduction.

claims.text: More strongly, for every fixed $`0\lt \delta\lt 1/3`$, a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT produces simple unweighted graphs that are three-colorable in the satisfiable case and have no independent set of size $`\delta n`$ otherwise, where n is the number of vertices.
claims.rationale: Exactly the deterministic polynomial reduction for every 0<delta<1/3 to simple graphs: 3-colorable versus no delta-fraction independent set.

claims.text: Proves $`\omega\le9/4`$ over ℂ, giving $`O_\varepsilon(n^{9/4+\varepsilon})`$ arithmetic operations for square matrix multiplication.
claims.rationale: omega(C) <= 9/4 with omega the infimum of admissible exponents counting arithmetic operations.

claims.text: In characteristic zero, some inner dimension na with a > 0.465 permits $`n^{2+o(1)}`$ rectangular multiplication.
claims.rationale: Dual exponent bound alpha > 0.465 stated only over C, not every characteristic-zero field.

claims.text: Further square bounds give ω < 2.258 outside finitely many positive characteristics and ω < 2.371054886006746 over every fixed field.
claims.rationale: All-field bound 2.371054886006746 stated; omega < 2.258 outside finitely many positive characteristics is not stated (only over C).

claims.text: Proves an $`\Omega(n^3)`$ lower bound for the border determinantal complexity of the $`n\times n`$ permanent over ℂ.
claims.rationale: Border determinantal size >= m^3/(5529600e) for m >= 1408 gives Omega(n^3).

claims.text: Even coefficientwise limits of determinants of affine-linear matrices require matrix size at least $`cn^3`$, for an absolute c > 0 and all sufficiently large n; the same bound therefore holds for exact representations.
claims.rationale: Coefficientwise-limit and exact representations both bounded by an explicit c m^3 for large m.

claims.text: Multiplies two n-bit integers exactly at every input length in deterministic worst-case time $`O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa})`$, with $`\kappa=2^{-182}`$, on one fixed finite-alphabet Turing machine with finitely many one-dimensional tapes.
claims.rationale: CONTENTS.md links no Lean scope note for this family, so it has no formal side.

claims.text: Establishes a randomized competitive ratio $`O(\log^2(k+1))`$ for k-server on every metric space, matching the worst-case lower-bound order.
claims.rationale: Universal C with ratio C log^2(k+1) for k>=2 on every metric with k+1 points; excluded cases trivial; lower-bound remark is context.

claims.text: One policy serves every finite oblivious request sequence, including on infinite unbounded metrics.
claims.rationale: One policy per metric and start serves all finite request lists on arbitrary, including infinite unbounded, metric spaces.

claims.rationale: Uniform bit machine on rational metrics with polynomial boot and per-request budgets in L and t, plus additive constant B.

claims.text: For every finite matroid known in advance, gives a distribution-independent online rule using one independent sample per element and earning a universal constant fraction of the expected offline optimum.
claims.rationale: For every matroid, a rule and seed law depending only on the matroid achieve a 2^-310 fraction with one sample per element.

claims.text: Values are independent and nonnegative, with finite expected optimum.
claims.rationale: Hypotheses: independent nonnegative coordinates, identical sample/value laws, integrable optimum.

claims.text: The guarantee holds even when the arrival-order adversary sees all samples, values, and the rule's entire random seed; no polynomial-time implementation is asserted.
claims.rationale: Arrival order is any measurable function of the whole outcome including samples, values and seed.

claims.text: Constructs a single language in deterministic polynomial time whose n-bit membership function requires $`2^{\omega(\sqrt n)}`$ total gates in unbounded-fan-in OR–AND–OR circuits, at every sufficiently large input length.
claims.rationale: Fixed polytime language whose depth-3 circuits eventually exceed 2^{A sqrt n} for every A, i.e. 2^{omega(sqrt n)}.

claims.text: This crosses the square-root-exponent threshold for explicit depth-three Boolean circuit lower bounds.
claims.rationale: Restatement of the previous claim, covered by the same target.

claims.text: Gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting perfect matchings in arbitrary finite simple graphs, with exact detection of zero counts.
claims.rationale: FPRAS for perfect matchings in every finite simple graph, zero output on every tape when the count is zero.

claims.text: Also proves the perfect-matching entropy conjecture of Anari, Oveis Gharan, and Vinzant, bounding the maximum entropy of a matching law at every feasible edge-marginal vector in a loopless labelled multigraph, including boundary points.
claims.rationale: F-(2-2/m)B <= H <= F for every polytope point of a loopless multigraph, boundary included.

claims.text: Gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting common integer bases of two integral polymatroids of equal total rank, supplied by exact rank-value oracles.
claims.rationale: Target counts common bases of two equal-rank matroids with independence oracles, not integer bases of integral polymatroids with rank oracles.

claims.text: Capacities are binary-encoded, each integer vector counts once, and oracle calls and bit operations outside the oracles are polynomial on every execution.
claims.rationale: Only the matroid (unit capacity) case with polynomial per-tape bounds; binary-encoded polymatroid capacities absent.

claims.text: For matroids presented by independence oracles, the results also cover common independent sets of prescribed, unrestricted, or maximum cardinality, even when the ranks differ.
claims.rationale: Only common bases with equal ranks; prescribed, unrestricted, maximum cardinality and differing ranks are not stated.

claims.text: For nonnegative integer matrices with prescribed row and column sums, gives exact uniform sampling in expected polynomial bit time and almost-uniform sampling in worst-case polynomial bit time.
claims.rationale: Exact uniform sampler with polynomial expected bit cost and worst-case polynomial almost-uniform sampler.

claims.text: The dimensions and binary-encoded margins are unrestricted.
claims.rationale: Quantifies over all m, n and natural margins with equal totals, binary encoded.

claims.text: Also gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting such tables with arbitrary individual cell bounds, including structural zeros, with polynomial cost on every execution.
claims.rationale: FPRAS with individual cell bounds including zero, zero output when infeasible, polynomial on every tape.

claims.text: For each characteristic, constructs in deterministic polynomial bit time a polynomial-dimensional matrix tuple detecting every nonzero division-free noncommutative formula of bounded size over any field of that characteristic.
claims.rationale: Hitting tuple only for characteristic-zero fields; construction time and polynomial dimension bounds not asserted.

claims.text: Rational formulas over ℚ also admit polynomial-size hitting lists whenever they have a defined rational-matrix evaluation.
claims.rationale: Polynomial-time machine outputs polynomial-size hitting lists hitting every admissible nonzero rational formula within the size bound.

claims.text: Proves that approximating Uniform Sparsest Cut within any fixed constant factor is NP-hard, even with nonnegative rational capacities and unit demands.
claims.rationale: Scope note says the result is an integrality gap, not a computational hardness theorem.

claims.text: The Goemans–Linial semidefinite relaxation also has integrality gaps of order at least $`\sqrt{\log n}/(\log\log n)^3`$, approaching the square-root-logarithmic upper bound.
claims.rationale: Sequence of unit-demand instances with OPT/GL ratio >= c sqrt(log n)/(loglog n)^3; integrality gaps are existential by nature.

claims.text: Disproves the modified integer round-up conjecture of Scheithauer and Terno: the integral bin-packing optimum can exceed its configuration linear-programming value by an arbitrarily large additive constant.
claims.rationale: For every c, an instance with configuration-LP values B and optimum > B+c.

claims.text: Approximating the optimum within any fixed additive constant is also NP-hard, even when every item exceeds 1/6 and each bin holds at most five items.
claims.rationale: Additive-gap NP-hardness for every c stated, but the item-size >1/6 and five-per-bin restriction is not visible in PackingGapNPHard.

claims.text: Proves the Courtade–Kumar conjecture: among Boolean functions of independent uniform bits, a single coordinate retains the most mutual information after independent bit-flip noise.
claims.rationale: I(f(X);Y) <= 1-h(eps) for all Boolean f and eps in [0,1/2], attained by dictators.

claims.text: A stronger theorem treats randomized binary summaries at fixed initial information.
claims.rationale: SoftContraction and SoftAttainment bound retained information for real-valued binary summaries at fixed initial information.

claims.text: The Hellinger conjecture is also proved for every Boolean output bias and noise correlation.
claims.rationale: RefinedBoolean gives the bias-dependent bound for every Boolean f and rho in [-1,1]; identification with the Hellinger conjecture assumed.

claims.text: Gives a randomized algorithm finding an exact maximum-cardinality matching in any simple undirected graph in $`(n+m)^{1+o(1)}`$ word time, with success probability at least 2/3.
claims.rationale: CONTENTS.md links no Lean scope note for this family, so it has no formal side.

claims.text: The time bound holds on every computation path.
claims.rationale: CONTENTS.md links no Lean scope note for this family, so it has no formal side.

claims.text: The same guarantees apply to finding a spanning subgraph with prescribed admissible vertex degrees, or deciding that none exists.
claims.rationale: CONTENTS.md links no Lean scope note for this family, so it has no formal side.

claims.text: For every fixed rational $`\varepsilon\in(0,1)`$, gives a randomized $`(1+\varepsilon)`$ approximation to unit-cost edit distance in worst-case expected time $`N^{1+o(1)}`$, with success probability at least 2/3.
claims.rationale: Fixed rational eps, (1+eps) estimate with probability 2/3 and expected work (N+2)^{1+eta} for all eta, large N.

claims.text: The strings have total length N and polynomially bounded integer symbols.
claims.rationale: Integer strings of total length N with polynomially bounded symbols, as in the target hypotheses.

claims.text: This is an asymptotic guarantee at fixed accuracy.
claims.rationale: Asymptotic bound at fixed eps matches the target form.

claims.text: A uniform decoder achieves quasipolynomial sample and running-time bounds for known fixed rational retention probabilities.
claims.rationale: Only lower bounds are formalized; the uniform quasipolynomial decoder is not stated.

claims.text: When the deletion probability is at most $`n^{-\varepsilon}`$ for fixed ε > 0, both bounds become polynomial in the input and parameter encoding.
claims.rationale: Polynomial upper bounds for small deletion probability are not stated anywhere.

claims.text: Resolves the three-processor unit-job scheduling problem of Garey and Johnson: a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm minimizes makespan for nonpreemptive unit-length jobs with arbitrary precedence constraints on three identical parallel machines.

claims.text: Arbitrary intersections of its parabolic subgroups are parabolic, proving the Parabolic Intersection Conjecture.
claims.rationale: Infimum of any family of parabolic subgroups is parabolic, for every Coxeter matrix.
